prompt: Our wallet service (NestJS + PostgreSQL/TypeORM) keeps an append-only, immutable double-entry `ledger` table — every transfer writes one `DEBIT` row and one `CREDIT` row, and `account.balance` is already maintained as an O(1) write-through cache updated inline in the same transaction. To guard against money being silently created or destroyed, we expose a `GET /ledger/invariant` endpoint that re-verifies `SUM(CREDIT) === SUM(DEBIT)` across the entire ledger on every single call, shown below. It's correct, but as the ledger grows to millions of rows this endpoint keeps getting slower, because it re-scans and re-sums the whole immutable history from scratch on every request even though almost none of that history ever changes. How would you optimize `checkInvariant()` so its cost stops scaling with the total size of the ledger, without weakening the guarantee that a real imbalance still gets caught?
